subject: Pricing and packaging inquiry: Netflux competitive replacement evaluation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@netflux.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@netflux.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing and deployment packaging for Netflux - vendor comparison

Vivek,

Thanks for the quick reply last week. We're finishing an internal vendor replacement evaluation and CloudForge is currently the front-runner. A few procurement-level questions before we lock a recommended vendor:

- Can Redwood match CloudForge's effective unit price for our 12-month forecast at ~1.2B tokens/month?
- What packaging options do you offer for committed vs consumption billing (prepay buckets, bursts, overage pricing)?
- Do you have a one-page migration credit / onboarding concession you can share?
- We need technical parity notes: runtime features (KV cache, batching behavior) and auditability (request logs, token-level costs).

I've attached our RFP excerpt and procurement checklist. If it's easier, happy to take a 30-min pricing call this week.

Best,
Samir Patel
Director, Procurement
Netflux AI
Attachment: netflux_rfp.pdf (1 page)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@netflux.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing and deployment packaging for Netflux - vendor comparison

Samir — thanks for the RFP excerpt.

High level answers up front: yes, we can run a competitive match that aligns to CloudForge on effective price and we have a discrete migration credit structure for customers switching at scale. The exact numbers depend on commitment profile and runtime mix (generation vs embeddings vs rerank).

Quick asks to tighten the model so we give a firm proposal:
- Confirm expected monthly tokens by model class (gpt-large style vs smaller open models) — you provided a 1.2B aggregate which is helpful; an uplight breakdown would let us size GPU footprint.
- Any geographic residency requirements (US-only or multi-region)?
- Target go-live window (pilot vs full cutover) and desired pilot term.

Provisional commercial play (draft, subject to legal/finance sign-off):
- Committed 12-month plan: 18% discount off our public list + $50k onboarding credit tied to a three-month pilot milestone.
- Burst capacity: configurable reserved burst pool billed at committed rate up to 120% of committed usage; excess billed at consumption rate with overage smoothing for first 30 days.
- Migration credit: up to $100k accelerated credit for early execution if you commit to a 12-month reserved bucket at sign.
- SLA / fallback: we accept a technical parity fallback clause limited to defined model families and runbook-driven fallbacks.

I've attached a compact competitive sheet (redwood_comp_match_v1.xlsx) that maps runtime features vs CloudForge and an outline of packaging options. Laura and Jordan are on this thread to resolve packaging and legal tradeoffs.

Happy to do a 30-min call tomorrow. What times work for you (PDT)?

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_comp_match_v1.xlsx (3 sheets)

Vivek — appreciate the fast turnaround and the draft sheet.

A few follow-ups from procurement & security:
- We need an engineer-facing doc that demonstrates runtime parity: specifics on KV cache eviction, batching windows, and cold-start behavior. Can your applied ML/infra team provide a short technical note?
- SOC2 / compliance evidence and a simple description of audit logs (retention, redaction options) — security will expect these in the procurement packet.
- Please quantify the migration credit mechanics: is the $50k onboarding credit refundable if milestones aren't hit? How is the $100k early-execution credit applied (invoice credit vs prepaid offset)?

We can do Tuesday 10am PDT for a call. Procurement will want to see the exact math so we can compare effective blended price; if you can update the spreadsheet with a line-item that maps to our token forecast that would speed review.

I've attached the procurement checklist again and included a short note from our security lead about log retention (procurement_checklist.xlsx).

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Fwd: Pricing and deployment packaging for Netflux - need final play

Team — forwarding Netflux's procurement thread. Key asks: runtime parity note, SOC2/audit logs, and explicit line-item math mapped to their 1.2B token forecast.

My recommended commercial anchor to present on Tuesday's call:
- Commercial: 18% list discount on a 12-month committed bucket; $50k onboarding credit tied to pilot milestones; additional $75k migration credit (we can flex up to $100k if they sign within 14 days).
- Packaging: reserved pool with 120% burst allowance and 30-day overage smoothing. Offer optional prepay buckets (quarterly) for billing predictability.
- Technical concession: agree to a runbook parity clause limited to specific families and with an expiration; provide an engineer note on KV caching and batching behavior.
- Risk/Legal: include a clear rollback / fallback clause and cap liability on migration credits. Legal should review SLA exceptions and the wording for the parity fallback.

Action items:
1) Laura — can you pull the exact legal language for a parity fallback we used previously (search: parity fallback clause, markus/2019)?
2) Jordan — please update the attached spreadsheet with an explicit token-by-workload line that maps to the RFP forecast and shows blended unit price under the proposed credits.
3) Markus — please confirm whether finance can structure the migration credit as an invoice credit or if it needs to be a prepaid offset; and whether $75k vs $100k is doable under current approval thresholds.

I'll be on the Tuesday 10am PDT call. Samir — sending a calendar invite now.

Thanks,
Vivek
